<!-- pr-reviewer: 05a25ccdd08224c5f111caf88d218722c39fb8bd -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (reviewed as the delta over #947; merge #947 first, stacked).

**What looks good**
- `list_features` now uses `pick::align::outward_normal` with `model::transform_of`. That helper turns the normal with the placement rotation only (`quat_rotate_point(loc.rot, n)`, `pick/align.rs`), never the translation, and renormalises it. A mirror is not representable in `Location` (pos + rot), so a rotated part is the case that matters, and the new test covers it (90 and 180 deg).
- The only change outside MCP is `pub(super)` to `pub(crate)` on `outward_normal`. The GUI/WCS callers (`pick/plane.rs`, `pick/mate.rs`, `pick/align.rs`) are untouched, so there is no behaviour change there.
- The fallback is documented on `outward()` in `mcp/features.rs`: a refused face keeps the canonical normal, placed by `world_dir`, so a listing never fails on one face. The duplicate winding helper is gone.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic`. The PR adds no dependencies and touches no process files.

**Local results** (delta over #947, PR head, own worktree target)
- `mcp_pick` 6 passed (includes `list_features_normal_follows_the_part_placement`), `mcp` 13 passed, `mcp_live` 10 passed, `mcp_setup` 6 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib pick` 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- Not run: GUI.

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The fallback arm `_ => world_dir(loc, fa.normal)` discards the refusal text. The comment names it, but the row does not say its sign is unverified. Consider a flag such as `"normal_verified": false` so an agent can tell a canonical normal from a winding-checked one.
- `outward_normal` is called per face and recomputes the winding. The author notes this for very large meshes.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 05a25ccdd08224c5f111caf88d218722c39fb8bd -->
**Independent review.** Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good
- `list_features` now reads `pick::align::outward_normal` (the helper the WCS and locate tools use) instead of a second winding derivation. Where it refuses (open, inside-out, mixed shell, no plane) the row keeps the canonical plane normal placed by the part rotation, so a listing never fails on one face; no unwrap/panic added.
- The new test `list_features_normal_follows_the_part_placement` and the #947 test `list_features_facing_follows_the_outward_side` pin top/bottom caps and the box (1 up, 1 down, 4 side) and the part turned 90 and 180 degrees.

Local results (trial-merged with main a6bd69d8, merge clean)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_pick --test mcp_setup`: 6 passed / 6 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Relation to #947
- This branch is stacked on #947: it carries #947's commit `0b14479d` (same files: `features.rs`, `mcp_pick.rs`, `mcp_setup.rs`) and its trial merge with main is clean. The two are one design, not two derivations: #947 supplies `facing` from the winding, this PR makes `normal` and `facing` come from the shared `outward_normal` and fixes the placed-part case (#956). Merge #947 first (this PR then shrinks to its own commit, a clean merge as it shares that commit), or merge this one alone - it already includes #947's change, and #947 then becomes a no-op. Either way no rework is needed by either.

Notes (non-blocking)
- A refused face (open or inverted shell) is listed with the canonical, sign-unreliable normal and no marker that it was not verified; a `normal_checked: false` style flag (or a refusal text) would let an agent tell. `crates/app/src/mcp/features.rs` `outward()`.
- `outward_normal` recomputes the winding per face, so a very large mesh with many faces is O(faces x facets); the PR body says as much. Worth a follow-up if listing gets slow.
- Curved faces return `None` from `outward_normal` and keep the canonical normal (as before).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
